notes.title: Developer's Note #3
notes.content:
Greetings from the Stargazers Studio!

We're continuing to pour our energy into development, driven by your ongoing support and interest. Whenever we hit a tough spot, your feedback and thoughts on the game keep us going, reminding us why we’re doing this. We truly appreciate your attention to our game, even though it's still a work in progress.

At the moment, we're focused on two main updates:
Firstly, we’re adding two brand-new scenes. Secondly, we’re introducing a new system designed to make your second playthrough after the ending even more enjoyable.

We can't share too many details just yet - we don’t want to spoil the fun when the update goes live.

The new maps we’re working on will offer a more visually engaging experience than before (just to manage expectations, they won’t include any nudity).

The new system will be simple, but it will let you enjoy previously played scenes in a fresh way (and just to clarify, it won’t be a conversation feature with AI integration).

If all goes smoothly, the system update should be ready by next week, with the new scenes following shortly after.

We'll be back with an official update announcement soon!
Though the world feels a little chaotic these days, we hope you’re finding peace in your own space.

— The Stargazers Studio Team

notes.title: Developer’s Note #2
notes.content:
Greetings from the Stargazers Studio!

We’re back with our second developer’s note. Lately, we’ve been working around the clock to bring you the best experience possible, fueled by all the support you’ve shown us.

Our goal is to roll out updates every two to three weeks, whether big or small, but as a small team, it’s definitely a challenge. Right now, as we briefly teased before, we’re working on additional episodes (days) for the game.

Originally, VR Secretary was designed to have around 8 to 10 episodes (or potentially more). The upcoming episode takes place before the current storyline and dives deeper into the secretary’s character. We hope you enjoy it!

Initially, we planned to release all episodes first and then focus on adding new features. However, many of you have been asking for more interactive content like outfit changes and a sandbox mode for extended gameplay. After this update, we’ll be prioritizing those features over episode releases.

Here’s what we have in the works:
[b]1. Wardrobe System[/b] – Customize the secretary’s outfits and see your choices reflected in the game.
[b]2. Photo Mode[/b] – Pose the secretary and take pictures. This feature will also be available in the main story mode.
[b]3. Conversation Mode[/b] – With an NLP engine, you’ll be able to chat naturally with the secretary. Her responses will change dynamically based on your words, actions, and even your relationship level.

Which of these features are you most excited about? Or is there something else you’d love to see? Let us know in the comments below!

We’ll be back with Developer’s Note #3 soon. Have an amazing day!

— The Stargazers Studio Team

notes.title: Developer Interview: The Making of the VR Secretary Game
notes.content:
[b]Q1. Can you introduce yourselves?[/b]
Hello, we are Stargazers Studio. As an independent, amateur team, we focus on developing games that are challenging for larger companies to create. Despite being an amateur team, we are made up of experienced developers, each with over 15 years in the industry.

[b]Q2. How did this project come about?[/b]
While there are many great VR romance simulation games out there, we felt something was missing. If the characters were beautiful, the interaction was lacking. If the interaction was rich, the story wasn't engaging enough. And, of course, the price for the volume of content often felt too high. So we thought, “Why not create something ourselves?” And that’s how it all started.

[b]Q3. Is the full version free?[/b]
Yes, when you purchase an Meta Quest and register a referral code, you receive a $30 voucher. At that point, you may buy something like Beat Saber, a well-known and proven game. But after a few YouTube tutorials, you'll probably run out of things to do. Good content is abundant, but most VR games are original IPs, expensive, and tend to have shorter playtimes compared to console or PC games, which makes it hard to justify the purchase. As a result, many people end up selling their Quest or storing it away. VR devices have made huge improvements, but the activation rate remains slow because users are stuck in this cycle.
When we started making our game, we wanted to create one that every man who buys a VR device would download and try. We still remember the excitement of unboxing our own VR devices. While one game can’t single-handedly revive the market, we wanted to create a game that extends that initial excitement a little longer. That’s why we’re committed to keeping the main game free in the long term. We hope you enjoy the experience as much as we enjoy developing it.

[b]Q4. How does the development team make a living? Does the fact that the main game is free mean DLCs will be paid?[/b]
Although we are an amateur team with other full-time careers, we can’t ignore the need for financial sustainability in order to continue updating the game. We might offer paid DLCs for additional characters, outfits, and other content. But for now, our main goal is to offer the main game with as much content as possible to satisfy players, and that will be free.

[b]Q5. Some players might find certain situations in the game uncomfortable.[/b]
It’s impossible to create content that pleases everyone. But it’s also true that the gaming industry has been going through some strange trends recently. For instance, portraying female characters attract criticism if they aren’t diverse enough or if they’re overly sexualized. This, in itself, is another form of oppression and a restriction of freedom of expression. While Western developers engage in moralizing, Asian developers are quickly taking over the market share. Is it because Asian developers are less "educated" in these matters? It's something to think about.
Ultimately, players want a fun gaming experience, not to listen to preachy messages from developers. They already get enough of that at work or school. While we understand that games are a form of cultural content with social influence, we believe there should be a balance. We don’t think our game crosses any lines, and we are committed to creating an enjoyable experience for all.

[b]Q6. What does Ailey Edition mean?[/b]
Ailey is an NFT project focused on character ownership. We were fortunate to connect with the project and incorporate one of their characters into our game. The character, numbered 1001, didn’t have a name, but the owner generously allowed us to use it, which we’re very grateful for.

[b]Q7. What are your plans for future updates?[/b]
As many players have pointed out, the current story is relatively short. Our goal is to add more content to expand the game’s volume. We’ll also be improving interactions with characters and fixing minor issues. We’re also considering adding new characters, outfit changes, and a photo mode. Ultimately, we plan to integrate an LLM model for interactive dialogues and simple tasks, transforming the character into something more like a personal assistant. Right now, there are no dialogues, but we’ve left out voices intentionally for this future upgrade. This way, players can have their own personal Android assistant.

[b]Q8. Is there any review that particularly stuck with you?[/b]
We appreciate all feedback, whether positive or negative. Just the fact that people take the time to play our game and leave feedback means a lot to us. That said, reviews that mentioned how the game has potential and that it’s an experimental project particularly resonated with us. As we’ve mentioned, Stargazer is committed to creating experimental games that you won’t typically find from larger companies, so it was gratifying to see our efforts recognized.

[b]Q9. Any final thoughts?[/b]
We’re still far from perfect, but we really appreciate the positive feedback we’ve received so far. The development team is energized and excited to continue working on the game. We’ll continue to put in the effort and strive to improve. If we could dream big, we'd love for our game to be something everyone who buys a VR device plays at least once, and for those who haven’t yet purchased a VR, a reason to do so.
